sections.label: Singapore food waste 2018
sections.summary: In 2018, Singapore wasted 763,000 tonnes of food, a 30% increase from 10 years earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2018, 763,000 tonnes of food were wasted in Singapore, a 30% increase compared to 10 years ago.

sections.label: Good Samaritans Food Donation Bill
sections.summary: The Bill protects food donors from liability if food safety conditions are met, aiming to reduce waste and increase food availability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Every year, for the past few years, we generated about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes of food waste and a lot of this food is still edible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Good Samaritans Food Donation Bill aims to encourage more food donation by protecting food donors from criminal or civil liability for any death or personal injury resulting from consuming the food donated, provided that certain conditions to ensure food safety and hygiene are met.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill will help reduce food waste and increase availability of food for redistribution to food-insecure communities.

sections.label: Annual food waste average
sections.summary: About 750,000 tonnes of food waste was generated yearly on average over the past five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: An average of about 750,000 tonnes of food waste was generated every year for the past five years.

sections.label: Food waste and Semakau Landfill
sections.summary: Food waste is 11% of Singapore's total waste, and Semakau Landfill is expected to fill up by 2035.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Food waste makes up 11% of total waste in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Semakau Landfill is expected to fill up by 2035.

sections.label: Food redistribution and recycling rate
sections.summary: It will increase food availability for needy families, while less than 20% of food waste is currently recycled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It will help increase availability of food for redistribution to needy families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We currently recycle less than 20% of our food waste.

sections.label: Household food insecurity study
sections.summary: A 2019 study of 1,200 households found 10.4% experienced food insecurity at least once in 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A study by the Lien Centre for Social Innovation and supported by the Food Bank Singapore found that in 2019, 10.4% of the 1,200 surveyed households experienced food insecurity at least once in the past 12 months.

sections.label: Study of Good Samaritan law
sections.summary: In 2021 the Ministry of Environment and Water Resources partnered with National Youth Council youth to study a Good Samaritan Food Donation law's effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2021, the then-Ministry of Environment and Water Resources partnered with youth from the National Youth Council's Youth Circle to study the effectiveness of a Good Samaritan Food Donation law.

sections.label: Restaurant survey on donation Bill
sections.summary: An RAS survey found 80% of restaurants support the Bill, 60% likely to donate if passed, and 20% neutral.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To encourage more food donation, we need laws to tackle the issue of liability." I am very glad that a recent survey conducted by the RAS on the Bill found that 80% of surveyed restaurants strongly support or somewhat support this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Importantly, 60% are very or somewhat likely to participate in food donation if the Bill is passed; and 20% were neutral.

sections.label: US Good Samaritan Food Donation Act
sections.summary: The US Bill Emerson Act grants protection from civil and criminal liability if food is fit, donated in good faith, without intentional misconduct or gross negligence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the United States (US), the Bill Emerson Good Samaritan Food Donation Act grants protection from civil and criminal liability as long as the food is fit for consumption and donated in good faith and if there is no intentional misconduct or gross negligence.

sections.label: Italy law and Singapore consultation
sections.summary: Italy had no safety issues in 10 years, recovering over three million meals; Singapore consultation showed 83% and 81% support waiving civil and criminal liability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In Italy, no safety issues have arisen in the 10 years since the passage of the law and their food banks have recovered more than three million meals and 23,400 tonnes of food products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I should also add that in Singapore, the public understands and supports waiving civil and criminal liability: 83% of respondents to our public consultation agreed that donations to food charities should be exempt from civil liability; 81% agreed that donations to food charities should be exempt from criminal liability.

sections.label: Four conditions for liability waiver
sections.summary: Food safety and hygiene remain top priority, so four conditions must be met before a donor can enjoy a waiver of liability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We agree that food safety and hygiene must remain the top priority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is why we will introduce four conditions that must be met before a donor can enjoy a waiver of liability.

sections.label: Four conditions for food donors
sections.summary: Food donors must meet four conditions to ensure food safety and hygiene before benefiting from the waiver of liability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Food donors must meet four conditions to ensure food safety and hygiene before benefiting from the waiver of liability.

sections.label: Food safety at donation time
sections.summary: The food must not be unsafe and unsuitable at the time it was donated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, the food must not be unsafe and unsuitable at the time it was donated.

sections.label: Donor liability shield conditions
sections.summary: A donor meeting these conditions is shielded from civil and criminal liability even if a beneficiary falls sick after eating donated food.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If a donor meets these conditions, even if a beneficiary falls sick after eating donated food, the donor is shielded from civil and criminal liability.

sections.label: Waiver after four conditions
sections.summary: If all four conditions are met, a food donor will enjoy the waiver of civil and criminal liability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If all these four conditions are met, a food donor will enjoy the waiver of civil and criminal liability.

sections.label: Other defences and operative date
sections.summary: The defendant keeps defences under other laws, and clause 5 limits protection to liability arising on or after the Bill's operative date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The defendant continues to enjoy any defence available under any other laws like those in the Sale of Food Act and the Penal Code.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I should also stress that clause 5 provides that the protection from liability applies only to liability arising on or after the operative date of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To increase safeguards for food safety and hygiene, the Committee considered requiring food donors to be accredited to enjoy waiver from civil and criminal liability.

sections.label: Accreditation not required for waiver
sections.summary: The Committee decided not to include accreditation as a condition for waiving liability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For this reason, the Committee decided not to include accreditation as a condition for waiving liability.

sections.label: Four conditions for liability waiver
sections.summary: To enjoy the waiver of liability, food donors must fulfil four conditions which safeguard food safety and hygiene.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To enjoy the waiver of liability, food donors will have to fulfil four conditions which safeguard food safety and hygiene.

sections.label: Workers' Party supports Bill
sections.summary: The Workers' Party supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For this reason, the Workers' Party supports the Bill.

sections.label: Part D food safety measures
sections.summary: Part D requires measures to comply with written law on food safety and good hygiene, such as NEA guidelines limiting catered food at room temperature to four hours.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Part D, for example, requires that measures be taken "to comply with any applicable requirement under any written law relating to food safety and good hygiene".

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is sensible and the circumstance that especially comes to mind pertains to the existing NEA guidelines for catered meals, which limit the consumption time of food at room temperature to four hours from the time it is cooked.

sections.label: Prior Good Samaritan discussions
sections.summary: Good Samaritan acts were discussed in Parliament on four prior occasions, in 2008, 2012 and 2014 by Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef, and in 2021 by Hazel Poa.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I also observed that this is not the first time that questions concerning Good Samaritan acts have been discussed in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This occurred on four prior occasions, in 2008, 2012 and 2014, by former People's Action Party Member of Parliament, Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef, and more recently in 2021, by the hon Member Hazel Poa.

sections.label: Anchorvale food collectors
sections.summary: Anchorvale welcomes about 130 collectors weekly, with ranks increased as living costs rose, and the House must be aware of food security struggles.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In Anchorvale, we routinely welcome an average of about 130 collectors on a weekly basis.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, their ranks have actually increased somewhat as the costs of living have risen and, as a House, we must be aware of the struggles with food security that are faced by Singaporeans that fall just above the threshold of assistance programmes but continue to struggle to stretch the purchasing power of their dollars.

sections.label: US Good Samaritan Act
sections.summary: In the US, the Bill Emerson Good Samaritan Food Donation Act has provided liability protection to donors since 1996.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the US, the Bill Emerson Good Samaritan Food Donation Act has been providing liability protection to donors since 1996.

sections.label: Other countries' food laws
sections.summary: Italy relaxed rules for donated food in 2016, France and Spain penalise food waste, and South Korea charges for food waste disposal by weight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In 2016, the Italians passed a law in the Senate to relax regulations for food donated, such as allowing companies to donate mislabelled food as long as these do not pose a safety risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: France and Spain, on the other hand, have legislations penalising food waste, compelling entities, such as supermarkets, to donate unsold food to charities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The South Koreans are charged for the disposal of food waste by weight, prompting them to treat surplus food more conscientiously.

sections.label: Food thrown away daily
sections.summary: More than two million kilogrammes of food are thrown away every day.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Every day, we throw away more than two million kilogrammes of food.

sections.label: Households lacking food access
sections.summary: The 2019 National Population Health Survey found about one in 10 Singapore households lack sufficient food access.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The National Population Health Survey, conducted by the Health Promotion Board in 2019, found that approximately one in 10 households in Singapore lack sufficient access to food.

sections.label: Semakau Landfill filling up
sections.summary: Semakau Landfill is more than half full and is projected to reach capacity by 2035.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Singapore’s only landfill, Semakau Landfill, is already more than half full as of the end of last year and is projected to reach capacity by 2035.

sections.label: Tax reliefs for food donations
sections.summary: The Government can consider tax reliefs for businesses that donate unsold or excess food to charities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government can consider implementing tax reliefs to businesses that donate unsold or excess food to charities, so that there is a stronger incentive for companies to do the right thing and redistribute their unsold or excess food instead of throwing it away.

sections.label: No Good Samaritan law needed
sections.summary: MinLaw assessed there is no need for a Good Samaritan law in emergency assistance, but will keep studying other jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As such, in the context of rendering emergency assistance, it is MinLaw's assessment that there is no need to introduce a Good Samaritan law, though MinLaw said that it would continue to study the experience of other jurisdictions and would review our position if the need arises.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: First, it deals with food donations, not emergency medical services.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: And second, as I understand it, Mr Louis Ng is moving the Bill because potential donors are hesitant to donate because of potential liability concerns.

sections.label: No hesitation or liability concern
sections.summary: Ministers for Law said people are not hesitant to help and liability is pitched at one's skill or expertise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The context of the Ministers for Law talking in the emergency medical assistance context was that there was not a need because people are not hesitant to step up, number one.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And number two, there is no major concern about liability because our law pitches the liability at your level of skill or expertise.

sections.label: Unobserved fear of liability
sections.summary: The speaker asks what is not observed: people not stepping forward due to fear of liability, and says no need exists if no particular need is seen.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: My question is, what we do not observe is all the instances where people have chosen not to step forward because of fear of liability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Perhaps Assoc Prof Jamus Lim would join me in encouraging members of the public to do so rather than debating this in a theoretical manner.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: If we do not see that there is a particular need, then there is no need to pass legislation or move a Bill.

sections.label: Tax benefits for food donations
sections.summary: Tax benefits for food donations, like those for charitable giving, could be effective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Tax benefits for food donations, like those already in place for charitable giving, could be effective.

sections.label: Mandating labels on donated cooked food
sections.summary: Beyond requiring donors to inform recipients about handling and consumption time limits, information labels on donated cooked food should be considered mandatory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Beyond merely requiring donors to inform recipients about handling requirements and consumption time limits, we should consider mandating information labels on donated cooked food.

sections.label: Liability protection for prevalent endeavours
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Bill explicitly extends liability protection to these prevalent endeavours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Does the Bill explicitly extend liability protection to these prevalent endeavours?

sections.label: Allergen labelling guidelines
sections.summary: To mitigate health risks from allergic reactions, the Government is urged to consider guidelines for clear and consistent allergen labelling within the Bill's framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To mitigate health risks associated with allergic reactions, I urge the Government to consider implementing guidelines for clear and consistent allergen labelling, wherever possible, within the framework of this Bill.

sections.label: Mass food poisoning incidents
sections.summary: Recent incidents, including mass food poisoning cases involving the Singapore Civil Defence Force Academy and Bytedance, are stark reminders of large-scale food handling risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Recent incidents, such as the mass food poisoning cases involving the Singapore Civil Defence Force Academy and Bytedance, serve as stark reminders of the risks associated with large-scale food handling.

sections.label: Mandatory training for food donors
sections.summary: The Bill could include provisions for mandatory training programmes or certifications for frequent food donors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Perhaps the Bill could incorporate provisions for mandatory training programmes or certifications for frequent food donors.

sections.label: Food security and waste impact
sections.summary: The question asks how the Bill's implementation will impact Singapore's food security, waste management and national sustainability targets like the 30 by 30 goal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How will its implementation impact Singapore's overall food security and waste management strategy and contribute to our national sustainability targets, such as the "30 by 30" food sustainability goal set by MSE?

sections.label: Protection for community fridges
sections.summary: The Bill should explicitly extend legal protection to community fridges and food rescue initiatives that reduce food waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill should also explicitly extend legal protection to community fridges and food rescue initiatives, which play a critical role in reducing food waste.

sections.label: Religious dietary needs and training
sections.summary: The Bill should include guidelines and legal protections for religious dietary requirements and mandatory training for food donors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Given Singapore's multicultural society, it is also equally important to respect religious dietary requirements in food donations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill should include guidelines and legal protections to prevent unintentional non-compliance, fostering inclusivity and confidence in the food donation system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It should also incorporate mandatory training for food donors, equipping them with the knowledge and skills needed to handle food safely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It can serve as a catalyst for positive change in how we approach food waste and food security.

sections.label: Legal protection for food donors
sections.summary: The Bill assures businesses and individuals of legal protection when they donate safe, surplus food to households struggling to meet food needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill assures businesses and individuals of legal protection when they donate safe, surplus food to benefit households that struggle to meet their food needs.

sections.label: Tax exemptions for regular donors
sections.summary: The Government could consider extending tax exemptions to businesses and individuals who regularly channel surplus food to recipients.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, the Government could consider extending tax exemptions to businesses and individuals who been regular in channelling surplus food to recipients directly or through intermediaries.

sections.label: Colombia food donation tax credit
sections.summary: The Global Food Donation Policy Atlas reported Colombia allows food donors a tax credit of up to 25% of donation value.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Global Food Donation Policy Atlas reported that the Colombian government allows food donors to claim a tax credit of up to 25% of the value of donations made to food bank members and other organisations that promote health, environmental protection, human rights and poverty reduction.

sections.label: Supporting hawkers feeding lower-income families
sections.summary: Hawkers providing affordable nutritious meals to lower-income families should be supported, with subsidies or stall rental rebates considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hawkers that are committed to providing affordable and nutritious meals for lower-income families are thus integral to strengthening the food security and morale of these persons in need.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These hawkers should be supported and I urge the Government and operators to consider extending subsidies or stall rental rebates to them.

sections.label: Public-private partnerships for food waste
sections.summary: The Government is called on to encourage corporations and suppliers to reduce food waste through tax incentives and support.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second consideration: public-private partnerships are vital for scaling food waste reduction efforts.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I call on the Government to encourage corporations and suppliers to reduce food waste through measures, such as well-designed tax incentives on surplus food donations and supporting companies that implement effective waste reduction strategies.

sections.label: Limits on annual food donor tax incentives
sections.summary: Sensible annual limits on tax incentives per organisational food donor are important, as adopted in the US and EU.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Having said that, to prevent potential misuse and ensure that the system encourage genuine efforts to reduce food waste, it is important to set sensible limits on the total amount of tax incentives available to each organisational food donor annually.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Such tax incentives have already been adopted in the United States (US) and various European Union (EU) member states in efforts to minimise food waste.

sections.label: Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill
sections.summary: The Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill safeguards donors with good intentions in the fight against food waste.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill represents a crucial advancement in the fight against food waste by safeguarding donors with good intentions.

sections.label: Bill aims to reduce food wastage
sections.summary: The Bill intends to reduce food wastage and increase food available for redistribution to food-insecure communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill intends to reduce food wastage and increase food available for the redistribution to food-insecure communities.

sections.label: NEA household food waste study
sections.summary: An NEA study found each household disposed of about 2.5 kilogrammes of avoidable food waste weekly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some years back, a National Environment Agency (NEA) study found that each household disposed of about 2.5 kilogrammes of avoidable food waste each week.

sections.label: Guidelines on food donation types
sections.summary: The Bill should include guidelines on food types not to donate for health and safety reasons, such as milk-based food and shellfish.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In passing this Bill, there should be guidelines on what types of food should not be donated, purely for health and safety reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some suggestions from a RAS survey include exclusion of milk-based food and shellfish – generally, food that easily spoils.

sections.label: Daily food waste thrown away
sections.summary: A 2022 SG Government article states Singaporeans throw away 2,000 tonnes of food daily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: According to a 2022 article on the SG Government website, Singaporeans throw away a total of 2,000 tonnes of food every day.

sections.label: Safeguards for food donors
sections.summary: Food donation providers meeting four safeguards would be protected from liability from recipients of their food.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In particular, in relation to providers of food donations, provided certain safeguards are met, they would be protected from liability from recipients of their food.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These are: one, the food must not have been "unsafe" for consumption when it left the control of the food donor; two, the food donor must inform the recipient of the handling requirements for the food so it remains safe for consumption; three, the food donor must inform the recipient of the food of the time limit for consumption; and four, the food donor should comply with food safety and food hygiene when handling the food.

sections.label: Daily food waste disposed
sections.summary: Last year Singapore disposed over 1,700 tonnes of food waste daily, including usable and edible food.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last year, Singapore disposed over 1,700 tonnes of food waste daily, including a lot of usable and edible food in good condition.

sections.label: Tax incentive for food donation
sections.summary: A tax incentive was suggested for MSE and the Ministry of Finance to consider.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Perhaps a tax incentive would be helpful and I hope that the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE) and the Ministry of Finance can consider this suggestion.

sections.label: Donor immunity encourages food donation
sections.summary: The Bill is expected to encourage more food donations because donors will have immunity from civil or criminal liability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, that does not release them from any criminal liability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, this Bill is expected to encourage even more donors and organisations to donate food because donors will have immunity from any civil or criminal liability.

sections.label: Clause 4 liability scope questioned
sections.summary: Clause 4 excludes liability for death or personal injury, and the question asks whether the Bill should also cover illnesses or other physical harms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Clause 4 of the Bill excludes civil or criminal liability in respect of any death or personal injury that results from the consumption of the food.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Given this disparity in the definitions used in the Bill as compared to the Sale of Food Act, is the Bill's scope narrower, focusing solely on death or personal injury, or should it also encompass illnesses or other physical harms as envisaged under the Sale of Food Act?

sections.label: Suggested Sale of Food Act phrasing
sections.summary: The speaker suggests importing section 2C phrasing to cover any illness, injury, other personal harm or death from donated food.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If the intent in this Bill is to be consistent with the Sale of Food Act, then may I suggest importing the same phrasing used in section 2C of the Sale of Food Act within the Bill, meaning to cover "any illness, injury or other personal harm or death" that results from the consumption of the donated food.

sections.label: NEA food waste statistics
sections.summary: NEA statistics show 755,000 tonnes, or 755 million kilogrammes, of food waste were generated last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: According to the statistics tabulated by NEA, 755,000 tonnes, or rather 755 million kilogrammes, of food waste were generated last year.

sections.label: Food Bank meals and Bill purpose
sections.summary: The Food Bank Singapore Ltd produced over two million meals annually in the past three years, and clause 3 sets out the Bill's purpose.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Food Bank Singapore Ltd has produced over two million meals annually in the past three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The purpose of this Bill, as set out in clause 3, is to reduce food waste and increase the availability of food for redistribution to food-insecure communities.

sections.label: Donor liability concern consultations
sections.summary: Consultations found donors' key concern is civil and criminal liability, and protection may be provided where food safety laws were met.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Through our consultations, we learnt that a key concern of current and prospective food donors is liability, both civil and criminal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We found that the balance of donors' and ultimate recipients' interests may be struck, by providing protection against liability for donating food where food safety laws in the handling of food have been met.

sections.label: Singapore food waste increase
sections.summary: Food waste in Singapore has risen by about 30% over the last decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The amount of food waste in Singapore has increased by about 30% in the last decade.

sections.label: Food import wastage and donation
sections.summary: Singapore imports 90% of its food, so it must identify wastage points and move unsold products to the needy, with cooked food eaten within four hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As a nation which imports 90% of our food, we need to invest more effort to identify points of wastage and work together to move unsold products to the needy expediently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For cooked food, for safety, they need to be eaten within four hours of preparation.

sections.label: Food donation laws experience
sections.summary: The experience of the US, Italy and other countries shows effective food donation laws can significantly promote food donation behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The experience of the US, Italy and other countries has proved that effective food donation laws can significantly promote food donation behaviour.

sections.label: Donor liability protection conditions
sections.summary: Donors are protected from liability for death or personal injury from donated food if four stated conditions are met.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Specifically, donors will be protected from liability for any death or personal injury resulting from the consumption of donated food, provided that: one, the food was safe and suitable at the time it left the donor's possession; two, the recipient was informed of any specific handling requirements that is required to ensure that the food remained safe and suitable for consumption after it left the donor’s possession; three, the recipient was informed of any time limits for the food's safety; and lastly, the donor complied with all food safety and hygiene laws.

sections.label: Authority for conditions and revocation
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MSE will look at a statutory board like SFA to ensure the four conditions are met and to revoke the liability waiver for breaches.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will MSE be looking at any specific statutory board, such as SFA, to be responsible for ensuring that the four conditions are met for the liability to be waived?

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Additionally, will MSE be the authority to revoke the waiver of liability if breaches, serious breaches occur?

sections.label: Penalties for serious breaches
sections.summary: The speaker asks if the Government has considered penalties for donors who seriously breach any of the four conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope the Bill can also address potential penalties if any of the conditions stated in section 4 is seriously breached to safeguard the public who are potential recipients, especially if they are the vulnerable communities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would thus like to ask if the Government has considered any potential penalties for the donors if any conditions set in section 4 have been seriously breached.

sections.label: Support for smaller food donors
sections.summary: The speaker says supporting smaller donors encourages broader food donation participation and expresses support for the Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Providing such support for smaller donors will encourage broader participation in food donation efforts, ensuring that even the smallest contributions can make a difference.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Their dedication and hard work in engaging with relevant stakeholders have been instrumental in shaping this piece of legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope that the Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill will become a pillar to sustain our collective work towards reducing food wastage, supporting food-insecure communities and fostering a culture of generosity and responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my clarifications raised, I support the Bill.

sections.label: Grants and local standards
sections.summary: The speaker proposes Government grants for adopting standards and training, and suggests Enterprise Singapore consider a locally tailored standard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To facilitate this, I propose that the Government provide grants to cover costs associated with adopting these standards and conducting necessary training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Furthermore, Enterprise Singapore's Quality and Standards division should consider developing a standard specifically tailored to our local context, ensuring it meets the unique needs of our community.

sections.label: Zhenghua food rescue since 2022
sections.summary: Since its September 2022 launch, about 7,600 kilogrammes of food have been rescued and redistributed to Zhenghua residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Launched in September 2022, we have rescued approximately 7,600 kilogrammes of food and redistributed it to the residents of Zhenghua.

sections.label: Carbon credits from food redistribution
sections.summary: The speaker says food caring organisations could issue carbon credits from redistributing food, and recommends digital solutions to track redistributed food waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Thirdly, Mr Speaker, an exciting opportunity arises for food caring organisations in Singapore to issue carbon credits by redistributing food.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The revenue generated can support FCOs in their recovery of logistical costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This initiative presents a dual benefit – reducing food waste and contributing to our nation's carbon reduction goals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To fully harness this potential, I recommend supporting FCOs in adopting digital solutions to effectively track the amount of food waste redistributed.

sections.label: Steps to maximise Bill's impact
sections.summary: The speaker lists three steps: grants for accreditation and local standards, hyperlocal CDC-based redistribution networks, and digital tracking of redistributed food waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To fully leverage these benefits, we should: one, support food caring organisations with grants for quality mark accreditation and Enterprise Singapore's Quality and Standards division should consider developing a standard specifically tailored to our local context; two, focus on hyperlocal partnerships and community-based redistribution networks, utilising the CDCs to enable hub and spoke operations; and three, support FCOs to adopt digital solutions to effectively track the amount of food waste redistributed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Such technologies will enhance transparency and accuracy in measuring their impact, enabling these organisations to capitalise on carbon credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These steps will maximise the Bill's impact, ensuring a more effective and sustainable approach to food waste and community support.

sections.label: Food waste tonnage figures
sections.summary: Food waste produced in 2023 was 755,000 tonnes, a gradual increase from 744,000 tonnes in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The food waste produced in 2023 was a staggering 755,000 tonnes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: That is a gradual increase from 744,000 tonnes in 2019.

sections.label: Food Bank rescues food
sections.summary: The Food Bank rescues more than 800,000 kilogrammes of food annually.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Just to name a few, the Food Bank rescues more than 800,000 kilogrammes of food annually.

sections.label: Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill purpose
sections.summary: The Bill encourages food donations by providing liability protection for donors, helping families in need and reducing waste and environmental burden.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   The purpose of the Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill is to encourage food donations by providing liability protection for donors, so as to help more families and people in need and reduce waste and burden on the environment.

sections.label: Community collaboration for food distribution
sections.summary: Collaboration between the community, Family Service Centres and food rescue organisations helps reach more low-income families, and the Bill would scale up food rescue efforts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Collaboration between the community and the Family Service Centres and food rescue organisations is important to reach more low-income families in a targeted way who would benefit from regular food distribution. : I am very eager for the passing of the Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill as this will help scale up our food rescue and distribution efforts in Singapore.

sections.label: Sengkang Food Rescue collection
sections.summary: Sengkang Food Rescue collects multiple truckloads of unwanted fruits and vegetables from Pasir Panjang Wholesale markets and other donors, storing them at its Fernvale facility, with about 20 to 40 pallets each Saturday.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our key partner, Sengkang Food Rescue will collect multiple truckloads of unwanted fruits and vegetables from the Pasir Panjang Wholesale markets and from other food donors and store them at their Fernvale facility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There are approximately 20 to 40 pallets collected each Saturday.

sections.label: Families collecting produce
sections.summary: Typically, between 80 and 100 families come by to collect the produce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Typically, between 80 and 100 families will come by to collect the produce.

sections.label: Partners donating household necessities
sections.summary: Sembawang Town Council, TreeDots, Saint Gobain, Smile!SG and MAD joined Sembawang West Branch to donate household necessities to augment the fruits and vegetables.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Besides Sengkang Food Rescue, Sembawang Town Council, companies like TreeDots and Saint Gobain and volunteer groups like Smile!SG and MAD, have joined forces with Sembawang West Branch, to donate household necessities like toys, books, frozen foods, pillows and more, to augment the fruits and vegetables.

sections.label: Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill hopes
sections.summary: The Bill is hoped to bring more food donors and Samaritans, replicate food distribution programmes, reduce food waste and help low-income families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Everyone looks forward to the third Saturday of the month and we are passionate about helping our residents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Hence, with the Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill, I hope more food donors and Samaritans will come forward to contribute.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: With the additional support, programmes like Sembawang West's food distribution programme can be replicated in other localities and to many more towns in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill will assist in the reduction of food waste, help low-income families, inspire stronger volunteerism amongst more Singaporeans and make us a more caring society.

sections.label: CFWG formation and members
sections.summary: The CFWG was formed in 2019 and comprises 15 private and public stakeholders including food charities, Government organisations and corporate partners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The CFWG was first formed in 2019 and today comprises 15 private and public stakeholders, such as food charities, Government organisations and corporate partners.

sections.label: FoodConnect Database launch
sections.summary: The initiative led to the FoodConnect Database, launched in 2022, giving food charities a consolidated view of household food support to avoid duplication.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Today, that initiative has led to the establishment of a FoodConnect Database.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Launched in 2022, the FoodConnect database provides food charities with a consolidated view of food support received by a household, thus facilitating better coordination and avoiding duplication.

sections.label: GSFD Bill introduction
sections.summary: The introduction of the Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill is a significant step forward to bolster food support efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The introduction of the Good Samaritan Food Donation, or GSFD Bill is a significant step forward to bolster efforts in the food support space.

sections.label: GSFD Bill donation encouragement
sections.summary: With the Bill, donated food quantity and variety can increase, and donors are encouraged to work with food charities to provide greater choice.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: With the GSFD Bill, we can look forward to an increase in the quantity and variety of donated food, as more businesses and individuals are encouraged to donate.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: With this Bill, I encourage food donors who are considering stepping forward to also work with food charities to understand the needs of food support recipients and donate in ways that provide greater choice, including healthier food options.

sections.label: Diabetic patients food needs
sections.summary: For diabetic patients, white rice and sugar in standard ration packs are of little help, inspiring efforts to give better.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: For diabetic patients, for instance, white rice and sugar, items that are often found in standard ration packs, would be of little help for them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: And that is why I have been so deeply inspired by the many big hearts that have been involved in this space, working hard to evolve our giving models, so that we do not just give but, more importantly, give better.

sections.label: Singapore food waste management measures
sections.summary: Singapore generated 755,000 tonnes of food waste in 2023, with regulatory measures and a new treatment facility planned.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The total amount of food waste generated in Singapore in 2023 was 755,000 tonnes, which accounted for about 11% of the total waste generated in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about my Ministry's broader goals in managing food waste.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We have set out regulatory measures in the Resource Sustainability Act that progressively require, from 2024, large commercial and industrial food waste generators to segregate food waste for treatment or conversion into useful products and to submit annual food waste reports.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Concurrently, we are building up our food waste treatment capacity through the construction of the upcoming Food Waste Treatment Facility, which will produce biogas and boost electricity generation.

sections.label: MSE SFA support GSFD conditions
sections.summary: MSE and SFA support including four conditions in the GSFD Bill that food donors must comply with for liability protection.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: To this end, MSE and SFA support the inclusion of the four conditions in the GSFD Bill that food donors must comply with, before the protection from criminal and civil liability can apply.

sections.label: No waiver revocation needed
sections.summary: The Bill does not require revocation of waiver as food donors automatically forfeit protection if they fail the four conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: To address Ms Ng Ling Ling's query on whether MSE would be the authority to revoke the waiver of liability if food safety breaches occur, the Bill does not warrant the need for revocation of waiver as food donors would automatically forfeit their protection under the Bill if they failed to meet any of the four conditions.

sections.label: SFA investigates food safety incidents
sections.summary: SFA will continue investigating food safety incidents and take measures to manage risk to donation recipients.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: In the event of food safety incidents, SFA will continue to conduct investigations to determine the facts of the case and take appropriate measures to manage the risk to food donation recipients.

sections.label: Strengthening SFA regulatory powers
sections.summary: MSE and SFA will strengthen SFA's regulatory powers through the upcoming Food Safety and Security Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: To better assure food safety in food donation activities, MSE and SFA will be strengthening SFA's regulatory powers through the upcoming Food Safety and Security Bill (FSSB).

sections.label: Extending food safety requirements
sections.summary: Food safety requirements in the FSSB will be extended to cover food donation and distribution beyond sale of food.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Given that similar food safety risks exist in both sale and donation of food, we intend to extend food safety requirements in the FSSB to cover food donation and distribution activities beyond the sale of food.

sections.label: Bill purpose food donation
sections.summary: The Bill aims to encourage food donation to address food wastage and food insecurity by waiving liability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Ultimately, the purpose of the Bill is to encourage food donation to address food wastage and food insecurity by waiving liability.

sections.label: Expired food not covered
sections.summary: Food donated past its expiry, best before and use by dates will not be covered under this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The donation of food past the "expiry", "best before" and "use by" dates will not be covered under this Bill.

sections.label: Community fridges liability waiver
sections.summary: The Bill does not rule out liability waiver for community fridges and food rescue initiatives if four conditions are met.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill does not rule out waiver of liability for community fridges and food rescue initiatives, assuming that the four conditions are met.

sections.label: Liability waiver for food donors
sections.summary: The Committee decided to waive liability only for food donors for now, not logistics providers, despite public support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The proposal received strong public support, with around three-quarters of respondents agreeing that logistics providers should enjoy protection from civil and criminal liability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Committee ultimately decided to take an incremental approach and waive liability only for food donors for now and not logistics providers.

sections.label: Public monetary donation protection
sections.summary: Food donation still enjoys liability protection if the monetary donation comes from the public, not the food recipient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If the monetary donation is provided from members of the public and not the recipient of the food, the food donation still enjoys liability protection under the Bill.

sections.label: RAS survey donation likelihood
sections.summary: The RAS survey found 60% of respondents very or somewhat likely to participate in food donation if the Bill passes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The survey conducted by the RAS on the Bill also support this, with 60% of respondents saying that they are very or somewhat likely to participate in food donation if this Bill is passed.

sections.label: Unsafe and unsuitable food interpretations
sections.summary: Existing interpretations of unsafe and unsuitable food under the Sale of Food Act will apply to this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The existing interpretations of whether food is unsafe and unsuitable, under section 2C and 2D of the Sale of Food Act, will apply in determining whether food is unsafe and unsuitable under this Bill.

sections.label: Four-hour rule and liability protection
sections.summary: Regulation 13A prohibits caterers from selling food after four hours, and this must be complied with for liability protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Regulation 13A of the Environmental Public Health (Food Hygiene) Regulations prohibit caterers from selling or supplying food for consumption after four hours from when the food was first prepared.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The four-hour rule is a written law on food safety and hygiene and must be complied with to enjoy liability protection under this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Committee decided, that good faith would introduce too much uncertainty for food donors on when they will enjoy protection, when uncertainty from the risk of legal liability is the precise problem this Bill is trying to address.

sections.label: Four conditions for donor certainty
sections.summary: The Committee decided four clear conditions will give responsible donors certainty and peace of mind about liability protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Committee decided that four clear conditions that donors can fulfil, to know that they enjoy liability protection, will provide responsible donors with certainty and peace of mind that is very much needed.

sections.label: Food waste segregation and reporting
sections.summary: Mandatory segregation and reporting of food waste took effect this year for large industrial and commercial buildings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The mandatory requirements on segregation and reporting of food waste came into effect this year for industrial and commercial buildings that generate large amount of food waste.

sections.label: Rejected mandatory requirements for donors
sections.summary: The Committee decided against some mandatory requirements raised by Mr Don Wee as they might burden smaller donors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Apart from the four conditions, the Committee however decided against having some of the mandatory requirements Mr Don Wee raised as they might be a burden for some donors, especially the smaller ones.

sections.label: Subsidies for capital-heavy equipment
sections.summary: One possible avenue for support is subsidies or tax incentives for capital-heavy equipment such as blast chillers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One possible avenue for support is to give subsidies or tax incentives for capital-heavy equipment, such as blast chillers.

sections.label: Public consultation on food donation
sections.summary: A public consultation found overwhelming majority support for incentivising businesses to institutionalise food donation activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As Ms Jean See shared, this could help incentivise businesses to institutionalise food donation activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We put this through a public consultation as well and an overwhelming majority of the public supports this.

sections.label: Smaller charities' accreditation concerns
sections.summary: Smaller food charities and community groups worried accreditation and training requirements may hamper their work despite significant public support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While the proposal received significant public support, smaller food charities and community groups expressed concerns that the accreditation and training requirements may hamper their work.

sections.label: Committee decision on accreditation
sections.summary: The Committee decided requiring accreditation for liability protections may unintentionally reduce food donations in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: After considerable debate – and it is a tough balancing act – the Committee decided that requiring accreditation to enjoy liability protections may again have the unintended effect of reducing food donations in Singapore.

sections.label: SFA briefing for food donors
sections.summary: A good start would be for SFA to hold a briefing session for food donors on the SFA guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, a good start which can be done very soon would be for SFA to do a briefing session for food donors on the SFA guidelines.

sections.label: Bill's legal protection conditions
sections.summary: The Bill provides legal protection as long as four conditions are met.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill does provide this legal protection as long as the four conditions are met.

sections.label: Rethinking throwaway culture
sections.summary: The Bill's key point is not just urging food donation but having people rethink Singapore's throwaway culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Miss Rachel Ong shared about how reducing food waste is a nationwide effort and requires a society-wide change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I have to stress that the key point of this Bill is not just about urging people to donate food but to really have people rethink our throwaway culture.

sections.label: Food donation legal framework
sections.summary: The Bill is a starting point for a legal and policy framework for Singapore's food donation ecosystem, with future improvements hoped for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The work of the Committee and the Government is far from done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill is only a starting point to create an effective legal and policy framework for the food donation ecosystem in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope that the learnings from this Bill will form the foundation for future improvements in our food donation landscape and I hope we will see an update in the next few years.

sections.label: Food insecurity and waste habits
sections.summary: The Bill is hoped to revive the Pioneer Generation's spirit against food waste and cultivate these habits in younger generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But let us not forget that there are also many Singaporeans who are not sure what or when their next meal will be.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope this Bill will bring back the spirit of the Pioneer Generation, the true champions against food waste, and cultivate these habits in our younger generations.

sections.label: Members' Room food waste reminder
sections.summary: Members are reminded not to waste food in the Members' Room, and the Sitting is suspended until 3.20 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Members are reminded that when you have your food in the Members' Room, do not waste food.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I suspend the Sitting and I will take the Chair at 3.20 pm.
